Proposition
[the Ricci form is symmetric]

↗ def:dc-ch4-4-ricci-form ↗ prop:dc-ch4-2-5

1. ch4:4The Ricci form is symmetric, $Q(x,y)=Q(y,x)$ for all $x,y\in T_pM$. In particular $\mathrm{Ric}_p(x)$ is intrinsically defined.
Proof

\sketch In an orthonormal basis $\{ e_i\} $ we have $Q(x,y)=\sum _i B(x,e_i,y,e_i)$. By the pair-swap symmetry (d) of item 2, $B(x,e_i,y,e_i)=B(y,e_i,x,e_i)$, hence $Q(x,y)=\sum _i B(y,e_i,x,e_i)=Q(y,x)$. $\blacksquare $

□
